content: The medication norgestrel, a progestin, is used to prevent pregnancy. It works by thickening vaginal fluid to inhibit sperm from reaching an egg, thereby preventing fertilization. It is not an emergency contraceptive and will not prevent pregnancy if used after unprotected sex. Additionally, it does not protect against sexually transmitted diseases (STDs) such as HIV, hepatitis B, gonorrhea, or syphilis. To reduce the risk of infection, it is recommended to use an effective barrier method, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during all sexual activity. How to Use: If using an over-the-counter product for self-treatment, carefully read all directions on the product packaging before use. If you have any questions, consult your pharmacist. Take this medication orally, with or without food, once daily. It is crucial to take the medication at the same time every day without skipping doses. If you experience stomach upset or nausea, taking the medication after your evening meal or at bedtime may help. Alternatively, you may choose a time of day that is easier for you to remember. Continue taking one tablet daily, and after finishing the last tablet in your current pack, start a new pack the next day. Your menstrual periods may vary in timing, duration, and intensity, and you may experience spotting between periods. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for guidance on switching from other forms of hormonal birth control, such as patches or other birth control pills, to this product. Side Effects: Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, increased appetite, stomach cramping or bloating, dizziness, and headaches. Vaginal bleeding between periods (spotting) or missed/irregular periods may occur, especially during the first few months of use. If these effects persist or worsen, inform your doctor or pharmacist promptly. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. This is not a complete list of potential side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before taking norgestrel, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other progestins (e.g., norethindrone), or any inactive ingredients in the product (e.g., tartrazine). This medication may cause dizziness, and alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. If you become pregnant or suspect you may be pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. A small amount of this medication passes into breast milk but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some drugs may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control by decreasing the levels of birth control hormones in your body, potentially leading to pregnancy. Examples include griseofulvin, modafinil, rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifabutin), and St. John’s Wort. Inform your doctor when starting any new drug and discuss whether you should use reliable backup birth control. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, potentially causing false test results. Missed Dose: Refer to the product package information for advice on missed doses. You may need to use backup birth control (e.g., condoms, spermicides) to prevent pregnancy. Storage: Store at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Notes: This summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
